residentNumber.privacyNote: The number is processed only in this browser. It is never sent to a server and is not stored in the URL, history or local storage.

status.checksumMismatchForeignerDesc: Foreigner registration numbers follow a separate scheme set by the Ministry of Justice (13 digits showing birth date, sex and registering office — Immigration Act Enforcement Decree Art. 40-3), not the October 2020 resident-number reform. The check-digit formula is not published in law, so a mismatch alone does not prove the number is invalid. Check for typos first.
status.validDesc: Both the birth date and the check digit follow the rules. Whether the number was actually issued cannot be verified.
status.checksumMismatchDesc: Numbers issued or changed since October 2020 use 6 random trailing digits, so the checksum does not apply and the number may still be valid. For older numbers this is likely a typo.
status.checksumMismatchAfterReform: People born after October 2020 receive numbers under the new scheme, which has no checksum. If the birth date and gender digit are right, the number can be considered valid.
status.invalidDateDesc: The first 6 digits are not a real calendar date (e.g. Feb 30, month 13).
status.futureDateDesc: The birth date is after today. Check the 7th digit (century code).

residentNumber.title: Resident Registration Number Validator
residentNumber.description: Validate Korean resident registration numbers (13 digits). Format validation only, no data is stored.

codes.title: 7th digit codes
codes.foreigner: 5/6: foreign male/female born in the 1900s, 7/8: in the 2000s

guide.foreignerNote: Alien registration numbers use a different check formula, (13 − sum mod 11) mod 10. This tool picks the formula automatically from the 7th digit.

reform.title: October 2020 numbering reform
reform.body: Since October 2020, newly assigned or changed resident registration numbers have 6 random digits after the birth date and gender digit. The region code and check digit rules no longer apply, so a checksum mismatch alone does not mean a number is fake. Existing numbers are unchanged.

guide.title: Resident Number Guide

structure.title: Number Structure
items: Numbers issued before Oct 2020: 8-11 region code of first registration, 12 serial, 13 check digit. Numbers issued or changed since then: digits 8-13 are random

validation.title: Validation Method
items: Sum all products, divide by 11, get remainder
Subtract remainder from 11, mod 10 = check digit
This tool performs algorithm validation only

whatIs.title: What is the Resident Number Validator?
whatIs.description: The Resident Number Validator checks the birth date, gender/century code and check digit of a 13-digit Korean Resident Registration Number, reflecting the October 2020 numbering reform. Nothing is sent to a server or stored; all validation runs in your browser.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Enter a 13-digit resident number in the input field (with or without a hyphen).
2. Validation runs automatically as you type.
3. View decoded information such as date of birth, gender, and nationality status.
4. If invalid, read the explanation of which rule was violated.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: This tool only validates the format — it cannot verify whether a number was actually issued.
To protect privacy, avoid entering real resident numbers unnecessarily.
Developers can use this to test the validation logic for registration form fields.

items.q: Is the number I enter saved anywhere?
items.a: No. All validation is handled by JavaScript in your browser. No data is ever transmitted to a server.

items.q: Why might a correctly formatted number fail the checksum?
items.a: For numbers assigned before October 2020 the last digit is a check digit computed from the first 12 digits. Numbers assigned or changed since October 2020 end in 6 random digits, so the check-digit formula no longer applies and a mismatch alone does not make a number invalid.

items.q: Can I also validate foreigner registration numbers?
items.a: Yes. Foreigner registration numbers have 5–8 as the 7th digit and use a different check formula, (13 − sum mod 11) mod 10. This tool detects them automatically from the 7th digit.
